issuer.name: not disclosed ('licensed partner institutions'; card issuance services by Signify Holdings, Inc. — 'Rain')

funding.supported_assets_note: Virtual Visa card in the Tuyo app that spends the user's USDC on Base: 'Pay with stablecoins anywhere', 'your funds stay under your control until you spend them'. Help centre: 'Deposit USDC or any token on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, or Polygon, then convert to Base USDC inside Tuyo'; only USDC on Base held in the 'Cash' section funds the card. USDC held in an 'Earn' strategy (third-party DeFi lending protocols, variable APY 'up to 4.0%', 'may be lower or negative') can also be spent unless the user disables it. Tuyo Inc. states it is 'not a bank, cryptocurrency exchange, or asset custodian'; fiat services (deposits, virtual account numbers) run through Bridge Ventures, Inc. Physical card: 'Coming soon' / 'in the works' — no date.

eligibility.nationality_restrictions_note: No nationality rule is stated on the pages read. Separate cardholder agreements exist for 'International' (last updated 2025-11-25) and 'United States' (last updated 2025-03-07) customers; both are hosted on about.tuyo.com (Notion) and could not be read by the fetcher.
eligibility.usage_note: The help centre says the card 'can be issued in most countries' and that 'a small number of countries and regions are not eligible', but publishes no country list — hence an empty allowed list outside the US and 'to_confirm' for every unlisted country. United States: available except in 19 named states — Arizona, Delaware, Georgia, Idaho, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Tennessee, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin ('a number of states and territories are not eligible'; territories not named). United Kingdom: every tuyo.com page carries 'This website and its services are not intended for, and should not be accessed by people located in the United Kingdom', modelled as excluded. EEA availability is neither confirmed nor denied on any page read. Fees are stated for 'USD purchases within the US' versus 'abroad', so non-US users pay the abroad fee on every purchase.

kyc.thresholds_note: No threshold: the card is only issued after a 'card application' that can be 'marked as rejected' ('A card application marked as rejected is final'). Wallet use without the card does not depend on the card KYC ('Funds remain under your control even if card KYC fails').
kyc.stages_note: Card application with identity check before issuance; the help centre says applications fail 'due to document issues, unclear photos, or unsupported occupation codes', so an identity document, a photo capture and an occupation declaration are collected. The verification provider, the document list and any level/tier are not stated on the pages read; the cardholder agreements (Notion) were unreadable.

access.note: 'Tuyo Card has no issuance, monthly or yearly fee.' No membership, subscription or token holding is mentioned on any page read.

fees.conditions: Fee table on tuyo.com/card: 'Issuance fee: Free'; help centre and FAQ: 'no issuance, monthly or yearly fee'. Applies to the virtual card; the physical card is not yet offered and has no published price.
'Monthly/yearly fee: Free' (tuyo.com/card); 'Tuyo Card has no issuance, monthly or yearly fee' (FAQ).

Funding = holding USDC on Base in the app's Cash section. No deposit fee is stated; the in-app 'Convert' of other tokens/networks to Base USDC, network gas and Bridge fiat on-ramp fees are not documented on any page read. Not treated as free.

Two stacked fees: '1% FX' on purchases in a non-USD currency plus '1% ABROAD' on purchases outside the US 'charged by the card provider' — 'UP TO 2% COMBINED'. USD purchases within the US: 0%. Modelled at the combined 2% because a purchase in local currency outside the US triggers both; a USD-denominated purchase outside the US pays only the 1% abroad fee.

The ATM article states 'ATM withdrawal fees and FX markups depend entirely on the ATM operator or the bank that owns the machine' and that Tuyo 'cannot know or control the exact fee'; it does not state whether Tuyo or the card provider charges its own ATM fee, so the fee is recorded as unknown. Withdrawals at 'any ATM that supports Visa' with the card set to Credit; 'Maximum per withdrawal: $250 USD' including any surcharge; 'Maximum 3 ATM withdrawal attempts within any rolling 24-hour period' (declined attempts count).

rewards.conditions: 'Buy Now, Pay Maybe': 'some of your card purchases are randomly free' — Tuyo may cover a purchase so it costs $0. No odds, cap, eligible merchants, regions, start or end date are published on tuyo.com/card, tuyo.com/rewards or the FAQ. Not a cashback rate; not modelled in the calculator.
rewards.description: Random full refund of some purchases ('Buy Now, Pay Maybe'), mechanics unpublished

limits.note: 'UP TO $50K/DAY TO START; UP TO $200K AS YOU SPEND': the daily limit can be raised to $100,000 once total purchases reach $50,000 and to $200,000 once they reach $100,000, from Card → Change limit after a first purchase.
'Maximum per withdrawal: $250 USD' including the ATM surcharge; 'Maximum 3 ATM withdrawal attempts within any rolling 24-hour period'.

editorial.summary: Virtual Visa card from the Tuyo app (Tuyo Inc., US) that spends USDC held in the user's own wallet on Base, with card issuance services from Signify Holdings, Inc. ('Rain') and an unnamed issuing institution. No issuance, monthly or yearly fee; 0% on USD purchases in the US, 1% FX on non-USD purchases plus 1% on any purchase outside the US (up to 2%); ATM withdrawals capped at $250 each (three attempts per 24 h) with the operator's fees on top. Daily limit $50,000, rising to $200,000 with use. Offered 'in most countries' and in the US outside 19 states; the country list is not published, the UK is excluded by the site notice, and EEA availability is unconfirmed. Its perk, 'Buy Now, Pay Maybe', randomly refunds some purchases without published odds.
good_for: Self-custody users who already hold USDC on Base (or on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon) and want a fee-free virtual Visa card in Apple Pay or Google Pay
US residents outside the 19 excluded states who spend mostly in USD at home (0% on domestic USD purchases)
not_for: Residents of the United Kingdom — the site states it is not intended for them
Anyone who needs a published country list, fee schedule PDF or cardholder agreement before applying — the agreements are hosted on Notion and the country list is not published
Non-US users who want 0% FX: every purchase outside the US carries at least the 1% abroad fee, 2% in a non-USD currency
Cashback seekers — no cashback rate is published; the only perk is random and unquantified
watch_outs: Issuing bank not named on any page read ('licensed partner institutions'); Rain is the card issuance services provider, not a bank.
'Buy Now, Pay Maybe' is a random perk with no published odds, cap or terms — it is not a cashback rate and is not counted in any ranking or calculation here.
Card balance held in an 'Earn' strategy (third-party DeFi lending) can be spent by default; returns 'may be lower or negative' and strategies 'are not bank deposits or covered by deposit insurance'.
Tuyo's own ATM fee is not stated; only the $250 per-withdrawal cap and the operator's surcharge are documented, so the ATM cost is recorded as unknown.
Top-up/conversion costs (in-app Convert to Base USDC, gas, Bridge on-ramp) are not published; nothing here is modelled as free without a statement.
Virtual card only — the physical 'Tuyo Visa Platinum' is 'Coming soon' without a date.
Cardholder agreements (International 2025-11-25, US 2025-03-07) and Terms of Service are on about.tuyo.com (Notion) and could not be read in this run.
